title: Vetala Extended Tale 48: The Two Sisters and the Wishing Well
summary: "Two sisters, Tara and Shanti, discovered a sacred forest spring presided over by a benevolent Yaksha. The Yaksha granted each sister a single wish....

full_text:
The king seized the Vetala once more. The ghost chuckled and said:

"Two sisters, Tara and Shanti, discovered a sacred forest spring presided over by a benevolent Yaksha. The Yaksha granted each sister a single wish.

Tara, ambitious and proud, wished: 'Make me the richest and most powerful woman in the kingdom, with everyone bowing before my commands.' Instantly, she was made a duchess with towering castles and chests of rubies. But soon, she lived in constant terror of assassination, surrounded by treacherous flatterers and envious rivals.

Shanti wished: 'Grant that whoever speaks with me finds peace in their heart, that sickness departs from homes I visit, and that our village fields remain fertile.' She remained in her modest cottage, but the sick were healed, quarreling families found reconciliation, and the entire countryside blossomed with joy.

Tell me, Vikram: which sister made the wiser choice under the laws of human destiny?"

King Vikramaditya replied: "Shanti made the far wiser choice. Tara mistook power and possessions for happiness, only to become a prisoner of fear and isolation. Shanti recognized that true wealth is the ability to dispel suffering and foster harmony. Her wish created a fortress of love and gratitude that no enemy could ever besiege."

"True to your name, Vikram!" laughed the Vetala, and soared back into the tree.
moral: Wishing for personal supremacy brings unending anxiety; wishing for the flourishing of others brings lasting peace.
